cap: An Rh-negative mother is sensitized by fetal red cells at the first Rh-positive delivery and makes IgM, which cannot cross the placenta, so the first baby is spared. In the next Rh-positive pregnancy, memory cells make IgG anti-D, which crosses and destroys fetal red cells. Anti-D immune globulin at 28 weeks and within 72 hours of birth or bleeding prevents the first step; ABO disease needs no prior sensitization and is milder.
